text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sam_oncall: policy-engine runtime panic while evaluating smart-routing rules. Service: smart-routing. Error rate spike in eu-west region.

maria: saw alerts + 5xx spikes for edges in eu-west, 10:23 UTC. getting paged.

sam_oncall: on it. can someone paste the stack/log?

henry: pasting the first 10 lines from logs:```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 423 [running]:
policy/eval.(*Evaluator).Eval(0xc0002b4000, 0xc0003a8000, 0xc0004b0000)
	/go/src/redwood/policy/eval/eval.go:212 +0x2a7
main.handleRequest(0xc0005c6000)
	/go/src/redwood/routing/main.go:145 +0x1f3
```

kevin: thanks. looks like a nil in rule compiled func. I see a user-provided expression with `routes[0].metadata.tags["preferred_variant"].length > 0` earlier in the trace. may be missing guard checks.

lisa: customer-impact: initial alert shows 3 customers with ~1000 requests/min hitting eu-west returned 502; region fallback attempted and created a routing loop for a subset of requests -> increased latency.

maria: tagging @product-oncall to kick off comms if it stays. product-oncall: do we have any high-ARR customers in eu-west at the moment?

product-oncall: quick list: AcmeCloud (priority P1), Finlytics (P2), BrightDocs (P3). AcmeCloud saw errors starting +2min after spike.

sam_oncall: immediate plan: 1) disable smart-routing policy evaluation in eu-west (fast fail to default model variant) 2) revert to last-known-good policy config 3) keep routing region-local while we investigate. I will run disable now.

ops-runner-bot: Executing: `redwoodctl policies disable --scope=eu-west --policy=smart-routing`
ops-runner-bot: OK: policy smart-routing disabled in eu-west (request id: r-8f1c).

henry: logs after disable show 5xx rate dropped ~90% in 30s. looks like fallback loop caused some cascading 503s before disable.

kevin: we should also block the auto-fallback rule that was bouncing requests between eu-west and us-east while policy expr throws. currently the routing fallback triggers when policy eval errors, but it's rolling to another region that triggers the same policy -> loop. I'll patch rule to not retry regions.

maria: sam_oncall can you confirm on-call rotation and who will own the postmortem?

sam_oncall: I'm owning immediate mitigation and triage. Henry will do root cause analysis with me. Kevin will PR fix for safer evaluation (nil checks). Lisa please coordinate customer comms with product-oncall.

product-oncall: drafting status update: "We are investigating a runtime error in our policy evaluation service that affected routing for several EU customers. Mitigation is in place and traffic is serving on default routing. We will update within 2 hours."

lisa: posted to status page and emailed AcmeCloud support contact. they replied: "Thanks. We're seeing recovery but please advise if we should divert traffic."

henry: for RCA: reproducer found. the policy expression used an index access on possibly-empty tags array: `routes[0].metadata.tags["preferred_variant"].0 == "redwood-large"` which after compilation produced an accessor without nil checks. Crash triggered when metadata.tags == null. Patch: compile-time guard insertion and runtime safe-access helper.

kevin: I'll open PR with tests and a migration that adds a lint rule to catch unguarded indexing in policies. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/compare/PR-2345

sam_oncall: next steps checklist:
- [x] disable policy in eu-west (ops-runner-bot confirmed)
- [x] stop auto-region-fallback to avoid loops (kevin patched routing policy)
- [x] contact top impacted customers (lisa/product)
- [ ] deploy safe-eval patch to policy engine (henry/kevin)
- [ ] run canary with synthetic traffic in eu-west
- [ ] postmortem schedule (sam+henry)

incident-bot: Incident severity: SEV2 -> downgraded from SEV1 after mitigation. Total impacted customers: 3. Duration: ~18m to mitigation.

maria: thanks team. Henry/kevin, keep me posted when patch is in canary. Sam, if anything regresses ping infra oncall.

sam_oncall: will do. I'll start the postmortem doc and add timeline. we should include: function-level stack trace, offending policy source, customers hit, and the fallback-policy config that enabled loops.

lisa: copying thread into #customer-communications channel for transparency. closing the on-call page in 10m if no regressions.

henry: adding unit tests now. expect canary deploy in ~45m.

kevin: also adding a lint rule + CI gate so this can't land again.

product-oncall: acknowledging. we'll prepare an FAQ for support.

maria: good work. leaving notes for postmortem.

sam_oncall: closing thread for now, will update postmortem link when ready.
